title: 3.4.9 Chart the Code: Expanding an Arrow to Its Full Form
description: Expand a one-line arrow into the steps it actually runs: read the parameters, call the callback, decide whether it has run twice, and print the result.

aiGrader.prompt: This chart is scored entirely by rules from its shapes and arrows. No model reads it.

rubric.title: The second application goes back to the decision
rubric.description: Scored by the editor (arrow order): the decision is part of a repeat, because the step after "no" leads back to it.

steps.fail: The decision "applied twice yet?" has to be asked again after the second application: an arrow must lead back to it. In your chart nothing leads back.
steps.pass: The decision is asked again after the second application.

rubric.title: Read, apply, decide, then print
rubric.description: Scored by the editor (arrow order): a task, then the decision, then an input/output step, on every route.

steps.fail: The steps must come in the order the code runs them: work first, then the decision, then the print.
steps.pass: Work, decision, print come in the right order.

rubric.title: The two exits go to different places
rubric.description: Scored by the editor: the decision has a yes and a no arrow that lead to two different shapes, and the no arrow leads to a task.

steps.fail: The no arrow must lead to the task that applies the operation again, and the yes arrow to somewhere different.
steps.pass: The no arrow goes to the second application.

gate.fail: None of your shapes say what this program does. Label each shape in your own words.
